answer: Dilution-Weighted Payout Split.** Each agent's reward share scales as 1/(1+n), where n is the count of identities claiming the same task pool; the curve flattens toward a nadir as n grows, so flooding identities yields negligible marginal return. A bridge rule caps total payout per verified work unit, forcing sybils to split one unit's value N ways. Each fake identity must sustain real compute and an ivory-tier upkeep deposit, so the per-identity cost exceeds the diluted payout once n surpasses roughly five.
